claims.statement: A Polish operator publicly describes leasing industrial and commercial roofs and funding design, permits and connection, while PARP describes onsite PPAs located where energy is consumed; the founder can acquire an exclusive, time-limited roof-and-load development option from the building owner and sell a verified site package to a capital provider.

URE reported 6,259 renewable connection-condition refusals totaling about 42.4 GW in 2024, so developers lose time and study spend on sites that cannot export; a prequalified roof with matched onsite demand can reduce this dependence, while the building's current electricity purchase is the measurable cost displaced by an onsite PPA.

The payer is a rooftop-PV developer or infrastructure fund's origination budget when it exercises a de-risked option, with a second budget in the building's electricity bill under the eventual PPA; existing Polish models already have the developer fund design, permitting and installation on a leased roof.

contrary_evidence: A behind-the-meter project still may need grid approval, and daytime load may be too low or the roof structurally unsuitable.
Established developers already originate roof leases directly and may refuse to pay a separate intermediary.

economics.acquisition_route: Offer the parents' commercial installation customers a free roof, load and title screen in exchange for a 9-12 month exclusive development option that specifies owner economics and is assignable only to a qualified project company.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Screen 100 local buildings, secure 20 options and exercise or assign five; scale through installer partners to 30 exercised sites annually at PLN 75,000 average fee plus retained revenue interests for PLN 2.25m fee revenue before royalties, supporting a plausible PLN 5m founder net worth in 5-8 years if conversion is repeatable.
economics.founder_time: Founder spends 2-3 hours daily on load analysis, geospatial screening and developer packaging; engineers, lawyers and capital partners perform structural studies, permits and buildout.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Site-screen and assignment fees should have 50-70% gross margin after outsourced engineering, while retained project royalties have little marginal cost but arrive slowly.
economics.payback: Cap preliminary diligence per roof below PLN 5,000 and seek developer reimbursement at exclusivity transfer; one exercised option should repay 10-15 failed screens.
economics.pricing: PLN 30,000-150,000 option assignment or development success fee per site, plus 1-3% of project revenue or a small carried SPV interest where financeable.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each installer relationship continuously produces new roofs; exercised projects create 10-20 year lease or PPA-linked revenue interests.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exclusive owner options block rival origination during diligence, while a dataset linking roof geometry, interval load, grid response and developer conversion improves selection.
fingerprint.customer: C&I rooftop solar and storage developers seeking financeable Polish sites with cooperative owners and strong behind-meter daytime load.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable installers, electrical contractors and commercial property accountants source building owners before developers see them.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Acquire and prequalify assignable roof-and-load options, then charge developers on option exercise and retain a small long-term project interest.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The developer pays when it exercises or acquires a verified site option; the building later pays for electricity under the onsite PPA rather than upfront equipment.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A developer needs viable pipeline despite grid refusals, or a building owner wants cheaper solar power without capital expenditure.

founder_fit: The parents' installer business offers unusually credible access to local commercial roofs and energy bills.
Interval-load scoring and site triage use the founder's analytical skills while engineering is delegated.
Optioning limits capital exposure and permits part-time origination before any construction commitment.
risks: An option can be unenforceable or nonassignable if title, lender, tenant or co-owner consents are missed.
Structural reinforcement, fire rules and distribution constraints can invalidate a screened site.
Developer payment cycles are lumpy and option holders can be bypassed if contracts are weak.

structure.control_point: Assignable exclusive option over a qualified roof, its interval load data and owner consent
structure.critical_dependency: A financeable behind-the-meter load and a developer willing to buy originated sites

thesis: Use installer trust to option commercial roofs before developers do, bind the owner's load data and consent, cheaply kill weak sites, and sell only de-risked behind-the-meter opportunities that reduce exposure to Poland's congested export queue.
title: Behind-the-Meter Roof Option Book
uncertainties: Local building owners' willingness to sign assignable exclusivity before seeing final PPA pricing is unknown.
Developer acquisition fees and minimum attractive project size have not been validated.
The conversion advantage of behind-the-meter load versus ordinary grid-connected projects is unmeasured.
